name: Daniel
overview: Daniel is a male prophet identified as the prophet of the book of Daniel, as noted in Ezekiel 14:14. There is no mention of his tribe or additional personal notes. His role as a prophet is central to his biblical identity.
namesAndTitles: The name Daniel means 'G-d [El] is my judge,' reflecting his relationship with God. He was also called Belteshazzar, meaning 'protect his life,' a name given in Babylonian captivity. Additionally, he is referred to by titles such as 'servant of the living G-d' and 'Son of man,' emphasizing his faithful service and prophetic role.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Daniel beyond what is listed in his unique attribute as a prophet. No familial connections are detailed in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Daniel stands as a model of steadfast faithfulness in exile, maintaining his devotion to God despite living in a hostile environment. His God-given wisdom surpasses that of Babylonian advisors, enabling him to interpret dreams and visions that reveal God's sovereign plan, including prophecies about future kingdoms and the coming Messiah. His life exemplifies faithful witness and trust in God's sovereignty amidst trials.
